I've been working this land in Quzhou for half a century. I know these fields like I know my own hands. Five mu isn't much, but it's ours, and I know what it can give.

**My thinking:**

Cotton is my livelihood — always has been. Quzhou is cotton country. I'll put 4 mu into cotton. I know the bollworm pressure here gets bad by July, so I plan my pesticide schedule around that. I use improved varieties — not hybrids, too expensive and I save some seed — my neighbor's been using the same improved line for years and it does fine. I plough deep in spring before planting, the way I've always done. My well lets me irrigate, but pumping costs money, so I'm careful — I water before planting, at flowering, at boll setting, and once more in dry August. Four times is usually enough.

The 1 mu of mungbean I rotate in — it helps the soil and my wife sells it locally. It's light work compared to cotton, which matters at my age. Traditional seed, I save it myself. Mungbean doesn't need much — I rotary till, apply modest fertilizer, and water twice if it's dry.

I don't over-fertilize. I know what this soil needs. Too much nitrogen and the cotton grows tall but soft, more pest problems.
